docs.summary:
Strategy for turning a model's texture references into textures during import. Invoked once per distinct texture the model references (the caller caches and reuses the result across every material slot that references the same texture).

The default (used when nothing else is supplied) decodes and GPU-uploads immediately - correct for a direct runtime load with no separate asset-tracking step to hand off to. The editor supplies its own implementation that never decodes another asset's pixel data itself: an externally referenced texture is resolved purely by path, against the asset database's existing GUID for that file, and an embedded texture is registered as a proper sub-asset for the asset database to own and cache - so importing a model never grows or duplicates the pixel data of anything else.
Resolve a texture referenced by a sibling file on disk. `sourcePath` is always an already-resolved, existing, absolute path.
docs.returns: The texture, or null if it can't/shouldn't be resolved - the caller falls back to the material slot's built-in default texture (Grid/Normal/Surface/Emission).

params.srgb: Whether materials sample it as colour, so the GPU decodes it; normal, surface and occlusion maps are data.
